entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.0 completes the release-readiness program: multi-root editor workspaces with an explicit Workspace Trust gate, editor profiles and per-file local history, approximate-nearest-neighbour local knowledge retrieval, and a governed Coding Workbench whose runtime actions are bound to the authenticated launcher session. Every autonomy-capable surface now reports readiness truthfully instead of showing green over an unusable gateway, and failed actions surface a diagnosable error instead of failing silently.

stateImpact.description: The local UI store migrates forward automatically on first start (schema 9 to 19). Migrations are additive: new tables for workspace manifests, workspace trust, editor profiles, local history, coding-runtime snapshots and memory autonomy policy, plus new columns on existing chat rows. No existing row is deleted or rewritten destructively. After the migration an older Keiko binary refuses to open the store rather than corrupting it.

Workspaces become explicit manifests with per-root trust decisions. An existing single-folder binding is migrated into a one-root manifest. The first time a workspace is opened, Keiko starts in Restricted Mode and asks for an explicit trust decision before scripts, language servers or agent execution are available.

Local knowledge retrieval moves to an approximate-nearest-neighbour index built on demand from the vectors already stored. Stored encrypted vectors remain intact and are reused, so no pod has to be re-indexed; only cached materialization state is discarded and rebuilt.

Coding Workbench state-changing actions are bound to the authenticated, launcher-attested browser session. A window that is not paired with the launcher can read status but is refused run start, approvals, stop/takeover and follow-up prompts, and the surface now says so instead of appearing ready.

releaseNoteBullets: Added multi-root editor workspaces with an explicit Workspace Trust gate: a new workspace opens in Restricted Mode until you grant trust, and scripts, language servers and agent execution stay unavailable until you do.
Added editor profiles, portable profile import and export, and per-file local history with a keyboard-operable timeline and honest restore.
Local knowledge now uses an approximate-nearest-neighbour index for retrieval, built on demand from the vectors already stored; existing pods do not need to be re-indexed.

Coding Workbench, Chat, Git, Prompt Enhancer, MemoriaViva and Quality Intelligence now report readiness and outcomes truthfully: no green state over an unusable gateway, no silent failure, and every refused action names its reason with a copyable support id.
Voice turns now carry their staged attachments and document context, and interrupting the assistant cancels only the answer it owns instead of blocking sending elsewhere.
Governed Git delivery authenticates on every network path, reports commit signing honestly, and distinguishes offline from authentication failures instead of reporting one generic error.

review.rationale: The maintainer explicitly commissioned the 0.3.0 release in the local session and directed the portable delivery scope (bundled Node.js and OpenCode sidecar for macOS and Windows). The entry covers the release-readiness audit programme tracked in epic #2802 and the implementation waves merged into dev. The approval evidence is the release owner's authored comment on the epic issue #2802 (comment 5225214175), carrying the version-bound phrase 'Approved-for-publish: @oscharko-dev/keiko@0.3.0' on a line of its own; the publish gate verifies the comment, its issue binding, the phrase, and the allow-listed author through the GitHub API (GitHub refuses self-approval of one's own pull request, so the solo owner cannot mint a PR-review artifact).

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.1 is the first public download release. It carries the same product as 0.3.0 and republishes it under a usable tag: the 0.3.0 GitHub release was withdrawn during verification and GitHub keeps that tag immutable, so the downloadable packages ship as 0.3.1. Nothing has to be uninstalled or migrated. An older build left running only occupies the local port, and the new one says so on startup and names both ways out (stop it, or start on another port). The governed one-click update does not apply to this release: its portable evidence declares the evaluation signing status, and the updater accepts only production-signed, notarized portable artifacts. Install it from the GitHub Release download; the in-app update returns once the signed lane ships.

stateImpact.description: No schema change relative to 0.3.0. A store created by 0.3.0 opens unchanged; a store from 0.2.x migrates forward exactly as 0.3.0 described.

releaseNoteBullets: First public download release: unsigned evaluation bundles for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows, with Node.js and the OpenCode sidecar included. macOS needs one right-click - Open on first launch; Windows shows the SmartScreen notice.
Load an existing keiko.config.json directly in the setup dialog instead of typing every field.
Upgrading from 0.3.0 needs no migration. If an older Keiko is still running it holds the local port; stop it or start this one with --port.

review.rationale: Republication of the 0.3.0 product under a usable release tag, directed by the release owner after the 0.3.0 GitHub release was withdrawn during verification and its tag became immutable. This single record also carries the portable runtime staging contract, unchanged from 0.3.0 (program epic and the same three targets, staging only): 0.3.1 is one release event with one owner approval, so splitting it across two records would need a second approval artifact for the same decision. The evidence is the release owner's authored comment on epic #2802 (comment 5230996334) carrying the version-bound publish phrase on a line of its own, verified live by the publish gate.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.2 carries the same product as 0.3.1 and completes its publication: the npm latest dist-tag points at the current release again, so a plain npm install delivers today's Keiko instead of a 0.2.x build. The release pipeline that blocked the 0.3.1 npm promotion was repaired end to end - the publisher verifies the four published downloads (three archives and the Windows setup companion) byte for byte against build-run artifacts fetched by their immutable ids (a rerun can neither substitute bytes nor block a verified release), no longer refuses over per-target evidence files, resolves its own operating conditions (release-owner allowlist, transport policy, provenance attestation only where an OIDC provider exists), and states every unmet precondition before the gate chain runs. The project README was rewritten around the product. Nothing has to be uninstalled or migrated; the governed one-click update still does not apply while the portable line ships with evaluation signing.

review.rationale: Completion of the 0.3.1 release event: the npm latest promotion was blocked by a defect in the publish verification itself, repaired in #3055, and the repaired pipeline requires a version whose tag can still carry a release. 0.3.2 ships the identical product with the repaired release machinery and the product-first README; the evidence is the release owner's authored comment on epic #2802 carrying the version-bound publish phrase on a line of its own, verified live by the publish gate.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.3 carries the same product as 0.3.2 and completes the npm publication both prior releases were denied: the byte-for-byte publish verifier crashed on the first empty file inside a build-run artifact (Node 24.18 rejects a zero inflate ceiling), so every governed promotion path refused with an unreadable-artifacts error while the GitHub release itself was intact. An empty entry now reads as proven empty - a stream hiding content behind a zero declaration still refuses - and the npm latest dist-tag finally follows the current release, so a plain npm install delivers today's Keiko instead of a 0.2.x build. Nothing has to be uninstalled or migrated; the governed one-click update still does not apply while the portable line ships with evaluation signing.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.4 repairs the Windows portable installation end to end (issue #3072): setup no longer flashes a console window and stops - the launcher distinguishes a double-click from a terminal start, launches the UI, and reports real failures in a native dialog instead of exiting silently (incomplete install, damaged app bundle, runtime that cannot start). The Start Menu entry is a real shortcut; a legacy Keiko.bat from earlier releases is retired automatically during setup, repair, and the first start after an in-app update. The Windows archive pipeline now refuses symlinks, NTFS alternate-data-stream names, encryption-marked and mistyped entries outright, and installer cleanup retries correctly under silent installs.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.6 delivers the Windows installation repair to end users. Installing on Windows now opens the app instead of flashing a console window and stopping; when a start genuinely cannot proceed, a native dialog explains it. The Start Menu entry becomes a verified shortcut with automatic cleanup of the legacy launcher file, and the archive pipeline behind the installer refuses hostile entries outright. The tags v0.3.4 and v0.3.5 were burned during this release chain (each froze a defective asset-build path discovered only by the release lane); 0.3.6 is the first version whose Windows asset build was proven green before tagging.

review.rationale: Completion of the Windows-repair release chain under the owner's standing direction from the 2026-08-11 working session. v0.3.5 froze the last two bare-cl spawners (the native test protocols, executed only by the release lane) inside the tag; the publisher binds assets to the exact tagged commit, so the tag is unpublishable. 0.3.6 carries the shared MSVC resolution in both protocols, and the evaluation lane ran fully green on the fix branch BEFORE this version was tagged.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.7 repairs installation with Yarn 4. The npm package now carries every private Keiko runtime workspace through tarball-local file archives instead of npm-only bundle metadata, so Yarn no longer queries the public registry for private packages such as @oscharko-dev/keiko-cli. The release gate now installs the exact staged artifact with npm and through a Yarn 4.9.1 npm-registry locator before publication.
releaseNoteBullets: Yarn 4 can install Keiko again: private runtime packages are resolved from the Keiko tarball instead of being requested from the public npm registry.
The release gate now installs and exercises the same staged package with npm and Yarn 4.9.1, including the CLI, SDK declarations, TypeScript runtime, and all private runtime workspaces.

review.rationale: The release owner directed an immediate 0.3.7 deployment after a customer reproduced the Yarn 4.9.1 installation failure. Issue #3100 records the incident, its root cause, the corrected artifact design, and the version-bound publish authorization.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.8 is a cleanup and bugfix release after the 0.3.7 npm recovery. releaseNoteBullets: The npm README no longer shows the paused Keiko for Quality review card, so package pages avoid empty review metrics while active reviews are disabled.
Release publishing docs now name the verified npm Trusted Publisher binding: workflow file `release.yml` with the `npm-publish` environment.

Third-party packages were refreshed within their supported release bands, including React, Monaco, editor/test tooling, transitive lockfile updates, and the reviewed `fsevents@2.3.3` install-script approval; npm audit and supply-chain checks are clean while Next.js 16.3, Vite 8.2, axe-core 4.13, ESLint 10, and TypeScript 7 remain separate migrations because the current dependency-review license and major-version gates intentionally block them.

0.3.8 carries the post-0.3.7 bugfix set already merged on dev, including chat handoff hardening, debug breakpoint reconciliation retries, contract/gateway validation fixes, and package/release hardening with libc-aware offline install-smoke native optional seeding.

review.rationale: The release owner directed this 0.3.8 release in the 2026-08-16 working session after trusted publishing was configured on npm. The release bundles the merged bugfixes since 0.3.7, hides the paused Keiko for Quality card, refreshes third-party package versions within their supported release bands, and corrects the npm Trusted Publisher runbook before publishing with the latest dist-tag.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.9 is a customer-hardening bugfix release for self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateways (for example LiteLLM behind a corporate CA). Knowledge Pod indexing no longer reports an answered embedding-endpoint error as "model gateway is not reachable", the embedding path carries HTTP status detail and the same CA trust as chat, a first failed indexing run no longer permanently blocks the pod, workspace reloads no longer surface deterministic 412 conflicts or resurrect closed windows, and the desktop shell fixes an aria-hidden focus violation. It also delivers the Dev knowledge-work readiness stack: honest gateway readiness probes, desktop chat turn-lifecycle hardening with legacy rejection cleanup, grounded catalog refresh fixes, quality-intelligence judge degradation honesty, prompt-enhancer German travel-intent scoping, and window focus-race fixes.
releaseNoteBullets: Knowledge Pod indexing against self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateways (LiteLLM and similar) now reports answered embedding failures with their HTTP status instead of a misleading "model gateway is not reachable", uses the same certificate trust as chat (system CA fallback), retries transient 5xx/408/425 answers, and recovers automatically after a first failed run instead of pinning the pod to a provisional embedding identity.

Workspace state no longer loses dirty snapshots to deterministic 412 conflicts on reload, closed windows stay closed after a reload, and the background-window modal lock blurs focused descendants before applying aria-hidden, fixing the Chrome accessibility violation.

Desktop chat readiness and turn lifecycle were hardened: readiness probes verify a usable assistant answer (content-part arrays included), unready models are rejected before persistence on every path, an omitted modelId prefers a conversation-ready chat model, rejected legacy requests leave no orphaned user message and restore chat recency, and cancellation during memory retrieval settles before any provider call.

Quality-intelligence runs whose judge prompts exceed the model budget now persist a visible judge degradation instead of presenting an unqualified success, run-progress strings are localized (EN/DE), and the prompt enhancer scopes German travel framing to planning intent so definitions, translations, and price comparisons are no longer rewritten as itinerary planning.
Window focus races were closed: a delayed text-entry focus is invalidated by any later window interaction, including resize grabs and pressed-and-held maximize buttons.

review.rationale: The release owner directed this release in the 2026-08-18 working session for a customer deployment the next morning, requiring flawless LiteLLM connectivity, Knowledge Pod creation, and HTML manual indexing. It bundles the merged LiteLLM first-run indexing remediation (#3208), the Dev knowledge-work readiness stack (#3204), and the complete post-merge review-finding repair wave (#3212), all integrated on dev with green required gates.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.10 is a focused patch release fixing the Knowledge Pod indexing dead end that survived 0.3.9 on self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateways: a pod pinned to the second of two gateway entries sharing one model id (a common LiteLLM configuration shape after endpoint debugging) failed every "Index now" click with a generic conflict, zero recorded jobs, and zero diagnostics. Indexing now uses exactly the provider the request resolved (including alias-repaired pods), and the silent failure branch is gone.
releaseNoteBullets: Knowledge Pod indexing no longer dies silently when the pod is pinned to one of several gateway entries sharing a model id: the indexing job now runs with exactly the provider the request resolved (including alias-repaired pods), instead of re-deriving it with a strict first-match lookup that could miss and fail with an empty job id, no job history, and no diagnostics.
The same repair unblocks full re-embed maintenance runs whose embedding model had rotated — the previous silent branch made exactly those runs fail without a trace.

review.rationale: The release owner directed this immediate patch release in the 2026-08-18 working session after the customer's Knowledge Pod indexing remained blocked on 0.3.9; the root cause (divergent provider resolution with a silent failure branch) is fixed and red-proven in #3214, and the customer deployment needs the repair the next morning.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.11 makes strict OpenAI-compatible gateways work end to end. Embedding requests now fall back to the minimal wire shape when a gateway answers HTTP 400 to optional extras (encoding_format, array input) — the failure mode that blocked Knowledge Pod indexing on certain LiteLLM/TEI deployments while chat and a plain curl succeeded. The fallback remembers a gateway's strictness, keeps one absolute deadline over the whole compatibility ladder, and reports coherent error causes. A fresh install also no longer rejects the first chat: conversation readiness is verified on demand at chat creation and send instead of requiring a manual readiness check in settings.
releaseNoteBullets: Knowledge Pod indexing works against strict OpenAI-compatible gateways: an answered HTTP 400/422 to Keiko's embedding request triggers a bounded fallback to the minimal wire shape (no encoding_format; array batches degrade to per-item requests), with per-endpoint strictness memory, one absolute deadline across the whole ladder, and error causes reported from the actual failing response.

A fresh install can chat immediately after saving gateway credentials: conversation readiness is verified on demand with the minimal chat probe at chat creation and send, honest rejections and observed not-ready states are respected without re-probing, and probe failures land as redacted operator diagnostics.

A field-twin end-to-end test drives the full fresh-install journey (credentials, immediate chat, Knowledge Pod, HTML+Markdown folder, indexing to vectors) against a simulated strict LiteLLM over the real production transports.

review.rationale: The release owner directed this patch in the 2026-08-19 working session after the customer's strict LiteLLM deployment surfaced HTTP 400 on Keiko's embedding wire shape and the fresh install rejected the first chat until a manual readiness check. Both repairs are red-proven, reviewed (13 findings fixed), and verified end to end by the field-twin journey; Sonar passes with 86.5% new-code coverage.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.12 makes conversation-model selection and Knowledge Pod indexing robust on gateways whose first-listed model is a special-purpose engine (for example an OCR model) and on slow, CPU-served hardware. The conversation default and the contextual-retrieval fallback now prefer models whose gateway metadata declares a chat-compatible mode, so a warm OCR model can no longer capture new chats or chunk-context generation. A failed readiness probe heals after a short cooldown instead of pinning the model until a restart, grounded Knowledge Pod questions verify readiness on demand, and the model list reports never-probed models as unknown instead of unusable. Indexing no longer holds one HTTP request open for the whole run: the start answers immediately and the panel follows the persisted job, surviving reloads. A gateway outage trips a circuit breaker after five consecutive transient failures instead of grinding for hours, terminal job status is honest about majority failures, discovery limits are operator-raisable and loudly reported when hit, the embedding path honours the configured provider timeout, and interrupted embedding batches resume behind their completed work.
releaseNoteBullets: New chats and the contextual-retrieval fallback default to a model whose gateway metadata declares a chat-compatible mode (LiteLLM /model/info); mode-less special-purpose ids (OCR, speech, reranking) rank last and cannot capture the default while warm — re-run the gateway verification once after updating so the mode metadata is stored.

Conversation readiness self-heals: a failed probe retries after a 30s cooldown instead of pinning the model for the process lifetime; grounded Knowledge Pod questions verify readiness on demand (the first pod question after a restart answers without any manual probe); the models endpoint reports never-probed models as unknown/usable instead of unusable, so the picker no longer empties after every restart.

Indexing runs detached: the start request answers immediately with the job id, the panel follows the persisted job (settling strictly on that job's identity), survives page reloads by re-attaching to the running job, and a duplicate start is refused instead of racing the in-flight run.

Gateway outages stop runs early and honestly: five consecutive transient embedding failures trip EMBEDDING_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE instead of grinding through the corpus for hours; a run where most attempted documents failed reports MAJORITY_DOCUMENTS_FAILED; an intact partial index stays retrievable instead of being blacked out.

Discovery bounds are operator-raisable via KEIKO_LOCAL_KNOWLEDGE_MAX_DISCOVERY_FILES / KEIKO_LOCAL_KNOWLEDGE_MAX_DISCOVERY_DEPTH (hard ceilings 100000 files / depth 64), and hitting a bound now surfaces a DISCOVERY_LIMIT_REACHED warning in capsule health instead of truncating silently.

Indexing throughput on slow gateways: the embedding path honours the operator-configured provider timeoutMs (it was silently pinned at 30s), and an expired per-batch ladder deadline carries completed embeddings into the retry, which resumes behind them instead of re-embedding from item zero.

review.rationale: The release owner directed this last-chance patch across the 2026-08-19/20 working sessions after the customer's dotsocr-first LiteLLM configuration on slow shared hardware surfaced default-model capture, restart-bricked grounded asks, non-convergent indexing, and multi-hour hangs on gateway outages. Ten repairs across PRs #3220 and #3221 were adversarially verified (two multi-agent passes), every behavioural change is red-proven, and the field configuration is covered end to end by twin journeys including a process-restart grounded ask and an OCR-first fallback election.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.13 makes model-role recognition model-agnostic. Keiko now takes a model's role from what the gateway DECLARES about it (a LiteLLM /model/info mode), not from a guess based on the model's name. A model a gateway declares as a reranking, speech, image or moderation engine is no longer stored as this gateway's embedding model just because its name resembles one — a field incident where exactly that happened bound a reranking endpoint to every new Knowledge Pod and indexing wrote zero vectors. Models Keiko cannot use are now reported with the reason the gateway gave, instead of disappearing silently, and every declared embedding model is verified with a real embedding request before it is stored, so an endpoint that cannot embed is never bound to a pod. The name heuristic remains only for gateways that declare nothing at all.
releaseNoteBullets: A model's role now comes from the gateway's own declaration (LiteLLM /model/info mode) rather than from its name. A declared reranking, speech, image-generation or moderation engine can no longer be stored as an embedding model because its id happens to contain a token like "bge" or "e5"; the name heuristic applies only where a gateway declares nothing.

Models Keiko will not configure are now reported with the declared reason in the setup dialog instead of vanishing without a trace, and they no longer consume slots in the discovery limit — a gateway listing many speech or reranking endpoints can no longer push real chat models out of the configured set.

Every declared embedding model is verified with one real embedding request during setup. A model that cannot answer is not stored as an embedding model; a model whose role you asserted explicitly, or that was already stored, is kept and flagged as unverified so a brief endpoint outage cannot unpin working Knowledge Pods.

Gateways whose /model/info route is unavailable, restricted or rate-limited continue to set up exactly as before by falling back to the plain model list; only a response in which every model declares a mode Keiko cannot use is surfaced as an error.

review.rationale: The release owner directed this fix after three releases failed to resolve a customer's LiteLLM deployment: indexing produced zero vectors because model roles were guessed from model names. The defect was reproduced locally against a real LiteLLM container with invented model names before any code changed, and the repair was verified the same way: the customer corpus indexes to 347 vectors with the job succeeding, where it previously bound a reranking endpoint and failed with zero. An independent adversarial review of the first commit found seven further defects, five of which would have broken working deployments; all were repaired and pinned before merge.
